## Question 1 (Dummy Coding)

a) Provide a list of at least three categorical variables that would be relevant to your research.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} For each variable, include what its levels/categories would be and whether it would be considered dichotomous or polytomous.

b) Select one dichotomous and one polytomous variable from your answer to Q1a.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} For each, provide the dummy codes that would be generated when using that variable as a predictor in a linear model. (Note that I want you to indicate what the value of each code variable would be for each level/category. To do so, you will need to select a level as the reference group.)

## Question 2 (Nominal Predictor)

Read in the `political.csv` dataset (on Canvas), which contains information about students' political activities.

a) Imagine that you want to use dummy coding to regress the `informed` variable on the categorical `voting` variable.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} Select a reference group for the `voting` variable and briefly justify your choice (i.e., explain why you selected that group). 

b) Run the regression model described in Q2a in R using the factor shortcut (so *no need* to calculate the dummy codes by hand using `recode()`). Be sure to tell R to use the reference group you selected in Q2a. *Optional challenge: Conduct an $F$ test on the results of your linear model to see if the overall effect of the `voting` variable is significant.*

## Question 3 (Interpretation)

a) Report the estimated value of each regression coefficient from your model in Q2b and provide an explanation of what it means (e.g., this coefficient is the mean of X or the difference between X and Y).{{< hp glyph="b" >}} Include the intercept as that is also a regression coefficient.

b) Calculate the standardized coefficients for this model.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} How are they different from your answers to Q3a? *Hint: Standardizing does not transform dummy codes.*

## Question 4 (Multiple Regression)

a) Fit a multiple regression model that predicts the `informed` variable from the categorical `voting` variable and also controls for the continuous `read_news` variable.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} Interpret the unstandardized regression coefficients from the model in Q4a (including the intercept). By interpret, I mean that you should report whether it is significant and also provide a description of what the estimate tells us about the relationship between the variables.

b) Use the `estimate_relation()` function from the \{modelbased\} package to plot the predictions of the linear model from Q4a. Plot the marginal effects of each predictor separately as well as the predicted values with `read_news` on the x-axis and `voting` as the color scale.

## Question 5 (Two types of effects)

a) Why are the `voting` dummy codes' slopes different in the models from Q2b and Q4a?{{< hp glyph="b" >}} Are these zero-order or partial effects, and how does that impact our interpretations?

b) In your own words, describe why a researcher might want to regress $y$ on $x_1$ and $x_2$ simultaneously using a multiple-regression model, rather than just regressing $y$ on $x_1$ and $x_2$ separately using two simple-regression models.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} When might they want the opposite?
